title: Sweet Day! So Cool, So Calm, So Bright
description: Sweet Day! So Cool, So Calm, So Bright in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: George Herbert wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 962 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Soul's Beauty Unfading”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sweet day! so cool, so calm, so bright, Bri-dal of earth and sky, The dew shall weep thy fall to night, For thou, a-las! must die.

lines: Sweet day! so cool, so calm, so bright,
The dew shall weep thy fall to-night,
Sweet rose! in air whose odors wave,
Thy root is ever in its grave,
Sweet spring! of days and roses made,
Thy days depart, thy roses fade;
Only a sweet and holy soul
While flowers decay, and seasons roll,

licence: Public domain: George Herbert died in 1633.
credits: Words by George Herbert (1593–1633), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
